builder_plan.scenario: A support or data assistant repeats work across related customer requests.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's memory change in a replay of past tasks, with separate memory per customer.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current memory pipeline plus a no-memory control using the same agent.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, stale memories, retrieval misses, response latency, and all memory maintenance costs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Prospective Memory for Proactive LLM Agents
summary: Pro-Memory replaces purely retrospective agent memory (conversation history plus retrieval) with a separated store of pending future intentions, each linked to supporting evidence and activation conditions, plus a gating step that decides when an intention becomes actionable and an experience memory distilled from completed episodes. The cost is additional architecture and orchestration: intention-state tracking, per-observation matching against pending goals, and extra LLM calls for activation assessment and episode distillation, all of which add latency, token spend, and implementation complexity. It can fail if activation conditions are mis-specified (missed or premature triggers), if the intention-actionable judgment is unreliable on real workloads, or if the agent's domain has few genuinely delayed intentions, in which case the overhead buys nothing over a simple task list.
rationale: The framework is implementable with a single GPU or API-based LLM and addresses a real gap in proactive agents, but the abstract reports only qualitative improvements on two benchmarks without effect sizes, so adoption should follow workload-specific validation.
technique: Prospective memory for proactive LLM agents
